story.label: story
story.title: A curated specialty collection
story.lead: A taste lab with a limited selection.
story.p1: coffee cherry is a taste lab. Each coffee is chosen for its origin story, clarity of profile, and ability to speak for itself.
story.p2: We do not dilute attention with an endless assortment. We roast slowly, tell stories honestly, and sell only what we believe in.
story.p3: A limited selection is not a lack of choice — it is focus. Honest roasting and characters we stand behind.

bloom.description: A light floral profile with berry acidity and a transparent body. A morning coffee for those who value clarity of taste.
bloom.story: Bloom was born on the slopes of Yirgacheffe, where cool nights and misty mornings shape delicate acidity. We roast it light to preserve the floral aroma and berry clarity — like the first breath of air after rain.

velvet.description: A smooth chocolate character with caramel sweetness and a velvety body. Coffee for a slow evening.
velvet.story: Velvet is Huila at its softest. Honey processing enhances sweetness, and a medium roast reveals cocoa and caramel. We named it so because the cup feels enveloping — no sharp edges, only depth.

santos.description: A warm nutty profile with natural sweetness and a rounded body. A versatile specialty for any day.
santos.story: Santos grew on the Cerrado plateau, where sun and dry climate create dense sweetness. Natural processing adds nutty warmth. This is the coffee that starts the day in our lab — calm, reliable, honest.

noir.description: A bold dark character with citrus acidity and berry depth. For those seeking intensity.
noir.story: Noir is Kenya without compromise. High acidity, blackcurrant and grapefruit. We roast it to preserve the drama of the profile: dark, but not heavy — like a night with moonlight.

ember.description: A warm spicy profile with deep dried-fruit sweetness. An evening coffee by the embers.
ember.story: Ember was born in the Antigua valley, surrounded by volcanoes. Volcanic soil gives spice and density. We hear smoldering coals in it: cinnamon, dried fruit, deep warmth — the last coffee of the day at coffee cherry.
